ddl:
CREATE TABLE Insurance_Agent (
    Agent_ID INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    Contact_Phone_Number VARCHAR(255),
    Hire_Date DATETIME,
    Name VARCHAR(255)
);

CREATE TABLE Customer (
    Contact_Phone_Number VARCHAR(255),
    Customer_ID INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    ID_Card_Number VARCHAR(255),
    Name INTEGER
);

CREATE TABLE Payment_Record (
    Payment_Amount VARCHAR(255),
    Payment_Method VARCHAR(255),
    Payment_Time DATETIME,
    Policy_ID INTEGER NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (Payment_Time, Policy_ID),
    FOREIGN KEY (Policy_ID) REFERENCES Payment_Record(Policy_ID)
);

CREATE TABLE Insurance_Policy (
    Agent_ID INTEGER NOT NULL,
    Customer_ID INTEGER NOT NULL,
    Insurance_Term VARCHAR(255),
    Insurance_Type VARCHAR(255),
    Insured_Amount VARCHAR(255),
    Policy_ID INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    Premium VARCHAR(255),
    FOREIGN KEY (Agent_ID) REFERENCES Insurance_Agent(Agent_ID),
    FOREIGN KEY (Customer_ID) REFERENCES Customer(Customer_ID)
);

CREATE TABLE Claim_Record (
    Claim_Amount VARCHAR(255),
    Claim_Time DATETIME,
    Policy_ID INTEGER NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (Policy_ID, Claim_Time),
    FOREIGN KEY (Policy_ID) REFERENCES Payment_Record(Policy_ID)
);
gold_question: The insurance company has multiple insurance agents, each with a unique Agent ID, Name, Hire Date, and Contact Phone Number. An agent can handle insurance business for multiple customers. Each customer has a Customer ID, Name, ID Card Number, and Contact Phone Number. Each insurance policy has a unique Policy Number, Insurance Type (Life, Health, Property), Insured Amount, Insurance Term, and Premium. Each premium payment requires recording the Payment Amount, Payment Time, and Payment Method. In addition, the insurance company needs to keep track of each customer's Claim Records.
